column1: # Golden vectors of the three model rules that protal (C++) and the trainer (scripts/machine_learning_cmdline.py) both
# implement. tests/test_GoldenModelRules.cpp checks protal's functions on every line, scripts/test_model_pmml.py
# (GoldenModelRulesTest) the trainer's: a change to one side that the other lacks fails one of them.
# One case per line: the rule, the case's name, then name=value fields, the inputs first and then the expected
# outputs. A list is comma-separated and VALUE*N stands for N copies of VALUE; a curve is x:y points, comma-separated.
#                    inputs q, prior; outputs rate (the sample's), adjusted (each q's probability); tolerance 1e-9
# FalseCallKnob      context::FalseCallKnob; FalseCallSamples(...).calls(fdr), one sample of the scores
#                    inputs scores, curve (the calibration), prior, fdr; outputs called (the taxa called, those tied at
#                    the knob's score included), knob (the lowest score called, "none" when none is), rate (the sample's,
# DepthKnobAt        profiler::DepthKnobAt(curve, fragments); knob_at(curve, sample_depths(...)), --knob's 0.5 without a curve
#                    inputs curve (log10 of the sample's fragments : knob), fragments; output knob; tolerance 1e-12
# How the values were made: by hand where the rule allows it (mean_is_prior and all_at_prior keep q, as the sample's
# rate is the prior's; the FalseCallKnob cases of four scores: the running means of 1 - p are 0.1, 0.3, 0.367, 0.5;
# halfway_in_log10 and the curve's ends), the others by a third implementation (Perl, of the C++ code's arithmetic),
# whose rates were checked against the fixed point of rate = (sum of the adjusted q + 20 * prior) / (n + 20) found by
# bisection (within 1e-11), and by hand on a few: one_likely_candidate (0.99329 + 2) / 21 = 0.14254, deep_sample
